name: André Souza
description: Engineering to make it work, creativity to make it different. Since 2013 I've been building end-to-end solutions, from APIs and integrations to apps and AI automations. My work goes beyond software. Feel free to look around.
skills-description: Day to day it's Node.js, TypeScript, React, React Native and PHP, with AI in almost everything. If the problem calls for another tool, I learn it.
journey-description: Two chapters, so far. At Rivelli I spent seven years turning every department's problems into software: 40+ applications and an ERP migration to SAP S/4HANA. At iScholar, since 2021, I've gone from engineer to leading a team. Along the way I did three postgraduate degrees, in Design Thinking, IT Management and Digital Storytelling, because code alone doesn't solve everything.

description: Lead the engineering team in charge of bug fixes, integrations and improvements on the platform. I set priorities, work closely with each person and jump in on the hardest problems.
More than tripled delivery with the same effort, using AI automations and MCP integrations built by the team itself. The model is now being rolled out to other departments.

Kicked off a cost analysis that, together with management, cut more than USD 3,000 a month across several areas of the company. The team now builds monitors that keep bringing costs down and platform performance up.
Rolled out error monitoring for the platform with the team, so the queue is now prioritized by data and SLAs.
Built in-house AI tools with the team that already serve more than one department.
Led the implementation and code review of the React Native app, shipped to the App Store and Google Play.
Ran complex projects from idea to production and took part in architecture decisions.
Became a technical reference for the team and helped other developers unblock their work.
Improved the CI/CD pipeline and kept the REST API and the app running across several releases.
Received the company's 2023 performance award for creativity and innovation.
Built and maintained, in PHP, core modules of a platform used by 100,000+ people a day.
Worked on the Pix (Brazil's instant payment system) integration and maintained the payment flows.
Shipped app improvements and partner integrations that helped win new customers and raise school satisfaction.
Owned the platform's REST API and the app releases on both stores.
Took part in UX/UI decisions, weighing user experience, functionality and performance.
Part of the team that migrated the company's ERP to SAP S/4HANA.
Extracted and organized data from the legacy system and generated the SAP import files.
Built the integrations with business partners, side by side with key users and SAP consultants, so each one met the needs of its area.
Delivered the whole integration layer documented and running.

As one of two developers, built 40+ internal applications used by 2,000+ employees, from finance and HR to logistics and export. From requirements with each department to deployment on the company's own servers.

Built a financing control system integrated with Brazil's Central Bank that recalculates interest daily (CDI, Selic, TJLP), and a product profitability simulator that leadership came to use when deciding the sales mix.

Took processes off paper: a payslip kiosk that freed HR from a manual task every month, an anonymous engagement survey with charted results, and a pre-registration app that sped up approval of new customers.
Brought ERP data to decision makers with dashboards and panels on TVs across departments, refreshed throughout the day, so everyone could follow sales and production goals.

Merged 7 requests from different departments into a single configurable app, including inspections of vehicles and equipment far from the maintenance shop. Less development time, maintenance on schedule.
Automated exports, data extraction and integrations with the ERP, partners and the fleet tracking system. I even got to control remote equipment with Arduino and Raspberry Pi.

projects-description: From an API to a game. Where the code is open, there's a link. Where it isn't, I explain how it works.

projects-list.name: Pão Nosso
projects-list.summary: Company breakfast, ordered straight from the bakery. A B2B platform where bakeries sign up through an API, publish their catalog and receive orders via webhook.
highlights: Remote MCP server: an assistant like Claude browses the catalog, compares prices across bakeries and places the order on its own, within each API key's spending cap.
Signed webhooks that don't get lost: the order and its notification are saved in one transaction, and a worker handles delivery with retries and exponential backoff.
Security from the first line: scrypt passwords, API keys stored as hashes, SSRF protection and idempotent orders.
Integration tests on a real PostgreSQL database, and a demo that starts the API, the worker and a test bakery with one command.

projects-list.name: Psychology practice with local AI
projects-list.summary: A patient tracking system built for a real practice. Patient data calls for care, so all the AI runs on the practice's own computer.
highlights: Session audio is transcribed on the machine itself.
A local language model writes each patient's summary.
Documents are stored and organized in Google Drive.

projects-list.name: A book turning into a game
projects-list.summary: A book about neurodiversity that I'm turning into a game. The characters have ADHD, autism and other conditions, and the game puts you inside situations many people live through without being understood.
highlights: I'm doing it all solo, from writing to code, with AI as a tool at every step.
